summary: Re-tested the /cementerio hanging vine canopy after the SMIL animateTransform fix. Logged in via 'Probar cuenta demo', waited for canopy to render, measured strand positions initially AND after 7s of animation. Result: 34 strands are spread evenly across the full 1920px width — 12 in left third, 11 in middle, 11 in right (min x=22, max x=1843). Distribution stays identical after animation cycles (no left-collapse). Screenshots confirm visually. Dino card click opens cemetery-profile-modal (pointer-events-none works). No console errors.
critical_code_review_comments: Vines.jsx fix is correct: <animateTransform additive='sum'> inside the translated <g> composes rotation with the existing translate attribute instead of overriding it (unlike a CSS transform animation on an SVG element which would override the translate presentation attribute). This is the right pattern.
Side VineSide components lack data-testid attributes; consider adding data-testid=cemetery-vine-side-left / right for future automated verification (minor).
test_credentials: Demo login via 'Probar cuenta demo' button on /cementerio
context_for_next_testing_agent: Canopy strand distribution verified programmatically by measuring each top-level <g> child's getBoundingClientRect within [data-testid=cemetery-vine-canopy]. Reuse this evaluate() approach for any future vine layout regressions. The user-reported left-bunching bug (CSS transform overriding SVG translate attribute) is FIXED via SMIL animateTransform additive='sum'.
rca of the issue: Previous bug RCA: A CSS `@keyframes vineSway { transform: rotate(...) }` on each strand overrode the strand's SVG `transform='translate(x 0)'` presentation attribute (SVG rule: CSS transform wins over the attribute), collapsing every strand to x=0 and stacking them on the left edge. Fix: removed the CSS animation and added an SVG SMIL <animateTransform attributeName='transform' type='rotate' additive='sum'> inside the translated <g>. Because additive='sum', the animated rotation composes with the base translate instead of replacing it, so strands stay at their original x positions while gently swaying. Verified with programmatic getBoundingClientRect() measurements before and after animation cycles.
